decisions.question: Item 4 (S149, S150): which existing samples carry the six renderer gaps (an anonymous retry, a duration above a second that is not whole seconds, a repeated input, one topic name under two variants, one name and variant under two type names, the characters &|[]')?

options.label: split: every_combinator takes the edge and topic gaps, escaping the characters
options.consequence: every_combinator gains one chain after its last statement (a merge of one read of the event topic every.count taken twice, a switchMap with an anonymous retry, a throttle of 1500 ms, a map by label, writes to every.retried of types int and String), so edges 0 to 21 keep their indices and G21's edits of edge 0 and edge 10 still hit a map and a debounce; G8's case for the sample must list the added edges; escaping gains one write to odd.it's [a|b] & c, reusing its to$Label stage

options.label: all in escaping
options.consequence: escaping would gain a switchMap, a throttle, a merge and four topics, mixing edge rules into the sample about text; G8 untouched

options.label: all in every_combinator
options.consequence: the characters would go into a topic name of the sample about edges, away from the sample whose doc comment is about text the renderers escape

options.label: findings or claims_only
options.consequence: findings feeds the G3, G7, G14, G17 and G23 cases, whose expected findings would move; claims_only would stop being claims only

decisions.chosen: split: every_combinator takes the edge and topic gaps, escaping the characters
decisions.why: Each sample keeps its subject: every_combinator is about edges and their labels, escaping about label text. checkout, forms and empty are excluded by the brief, and findings and claims_only would disturb other cases. Appending the chain keeps every existing edge index, so only G8's listing of every_combinator changes; S154's suite passes 56/56 against the shipped package and the package's 371 tests pass.
evidence: docs/auto-run/experiments/sweep-topology-ir-cases/output.txt steps P, B and D (R4 to R17)

decisions.question: How are the extended samples' valid/ documents and render/ goldens derived, given that the shipped renderer's output must not simply be taken?

options.label: an independent checker, then the producer compared
options.consequence: independent.py derives the two documents from HEAD's plus the additions written out by hand from the declarations, and every golden from the documents by the contract's rendering rules; it reproduces all 15 files of the five untouched samples and HEAD's four goldens of the two extended ones; the producer's encoder and renderers must then give the same files (G19, G22, the package's tests)

options.label: by hand
options.consequence: about 200 changed lines of goldens retyped, with renumbered topic ids; error-prone and no cheaper to review

options.label: the producer's output
options.consequence: forbidden by the brief: a renderer defect would be baked into the golden

decisions.chosen: an independent checker, then the producer compared
decisions.why: The checker shares no code with the package and is validated by reproducing every committed file it can; the replay then shows the shipped encoder and renderers agree byte for byte with what it wrote. The Mermaid and Graphviz parse of the two extended goldens could not be repeated: the render-check tool needs npm packages that are not in the local cache (npm ci --offline: ENOTCACHED), and the run makes no network action beyond pub.dev.
evidence: docs/auto-run/experiments/sweep-topology-ir-cases/output.txt step I (0 differences) and step P (G19, G22 inside 56 passed)

decisions.question: Item 5, optional pins of text S153 settled: which are cheap enough to add?

options.label: G9, G20 and G21; not G8
options.consequence: three cases inside the one conformance library (an extension Doubling and an extension type Cents declared beside the samples); G8's pin is left, because two state topics whose value types render alike need two classes of one name, so a second library in behavior/, which holds only conformance libraries and bindings today

options.consequence: a third kind of file in behavior/ (a helper library neither suite nor binding), a structural choice for the fixture layout beyond a compatible case

options.label: none
